observations: grip() applies the same MCP/PIP/DIP target angles to index, middle, ring and pinky chains (70/88/55 degrees times one amount).
The thumb uses fixed flexion targets rather than an object-size/position-driven opposition solve.
close_on_handle() performs contact-limited closure along one parallel hinge axis per chain and uses one shared handle radius of 0.017 m.
curl_handle and pullup_bar both use the same handle-placement/contact machinery even though grip orientation/load path differ.
current_architecture_observation.interpretation: These are implementation facts, not proof of the visible defect by themselves. The owner-rejected r95 grip images and issue ledger remain the visual defect authority.

design_requirements: Finger closure must be contact/equipment-geometry driven and allow inter-digit differences; do not preserve one uniform four-finger curl profile merely for symmetry.
Thumb opposition, CMC/abduction behaviour and flexion must adapt to object geometry/relative position and produce a plausible opposing contact rather than only extra hinge flexion.
Forearm pronation/supination and wrist orientation are part of the grip/load path; avoid solving fingers independently of wrist/forearm configuration.
The same first-party solver must generalise across dumbbell handle, pull-up bar and other cylindrical equipment sizes without exercise-name-specific anatomy patches.
Joint limits remain deterministic and biomechanically bounded; contact convergence may stop a joint before its nominal target.
Left/right behaviour is mirror-consistent while permitting the measured/posed load path to differ when the task is asymmetric.
Palm arch/thenar and digit soft-tissue deformation must remain continuous with the wrist/forearm and must not rely on rigid bone motion alone.

required_probe_families.name: cylindrical_diameter_response
required_probe_families.purpose: Prove that digit flexion/opposition responds to equipment diameter instead of replaying one fixed curl.

required_probe_families.name: forearm_orientation_response
required_probe_families.purpose: Prove wrist/forearm/grip coupling and reject a detached hand solution.

required_probe_families.name: loaded_pushup_wrist
required_probe_families.purpose: Prove the wrist/load path and palm-floor transition under closed-chain loading.

required_probe_families.name: curl_handle
required_probe_families.purpose: Prove dumbbell contact, sequential digit wrap, thumb opposition and stable wrist through the motion.

required_probe_families.name: pullup_bar
required_probe_families.purpose: Prove pronated/supinated bar variants where supported, no contact drift and plausible wrist/forearm coupling.

numerical: contact/penetration metrics using the existing production contact model
left/right mirror audit where the task is symmetric
whole-body regression comparison against the accepted parent candidate
visual: non-uniform but anatomically plausible digit wrap
no handle through skin or visibly floating grip
wrist alignment with forearm and equipment force path
no forearm candy-wrapper twist or abrupt wrist seam

implementation_order: Reproduce the current candidate grip/wrist evidence and hash-bind it before edits.
Instrument per-digit joint angles, handle distance/contact and wrist/forearm orientation throughout the probe families.
Separate nominal human grasp intent from contact convergence so equipment geometry can stop each digit independently.
Add object-size/relative-position-aware thumb opposition before tuning cosmetic hand surface behaviour.
Validate the forearm/wrist load path in curl, pull-up and push-up before fitting any hand corrective.
Only after skeletal/contact behaviour is plausible, fit local first-party soft-tissue/palm correctives if evidence still requires them.
Run candidate-bound visual, numerical and whole-body regression evidence; close WB-GRP-009/WB-WRI-010 only with structured issue receipts.
forbidden_shortcuts: Do not close the issues because old numerical grip gates pass.
Do not use exercise-name-specific finger angles to imitate one screenshot.
Do not copy third-party hand meshes, rigs, animation clips or reference media into production assets.
Do not solve penetration by moving the equipment away from the anatomically intended hand contact.
Do not proceed to Phase 4 while either WB-GRP-009 or WB-WRI-010 remains a Critical/High blocker.
